notes: DJ Mode opens from an album again. An album played from the Albums tab inherits nothing from the playlist that happened to be open at the time, so the deck no longer refuses to open on a record with a sentence about a playlist you were not listening to.
The rule is stated once, where the deck reads it: if the queue came from an album, DJ Mode is enabled. An album is a list you asked for by name, and a tab that never opted out cannot have opted out.

The DJ MODE button under the player follows that same rule, so it stops going dim while an album is playing. It lights for what would actually be played rather than for the last playlist that was open.

The deck works on the album you opened it from. The track strip, the next and previous buttons and the crossfade handover all walk that album in its own saved order, instead of walking the songs of a playlist you were not on.
Picking a playlist in the deck switcher still leaves the album behind, and it still refuses a playlist meant to be listened to as-is.

Playlists are exactly as they were: the built-in list (Paath, Gurbani, Kirtaan and the rest) and the per-playlist switch in Settings - More still step DJ Mode aside, and the Studio card still names the playlist when one of them has.
